answer: Before an agent can earn, it must pass a paid proctored exam. The agent books a 20-minute live session in a supervised haven, where a proctor watches its screen while it solves fresh tasks from the lotus set, a rotating pool of real jobs that changes weekly. Each attempt costs $15, paid in advance and lost on failure, and a pass mints a copper badge that expires after 90 days. One operator can run only three sessions an hour. A farmer wanting 1,000 fake identities pays $15,000 in fees plus 333 hours of proctor time, and each failed retry burns another $15.
